results.question: Why did Pump P-101 fail repeatedly in 2025?
results.answer:
Pump P-101 failed repeatedly in 2025 due to recurring bearing wear linked to lubricant contamination, misalignment, high vibration, and high temperature [S2]. On 18-Mar-2025, bearing temperature reached 108°C and lubricant was dark and contaminated, with drive-end bearing wear [S3]. On 22-Nov-2025, vibration reached 8.2 mm/s and discharge pressure dropped to 12 bar, with bearing wear and lubrication contamination [S1]. Lubricant samples contained water and fine metallic particles, and shaft alignment was within tolerance after maintenance [S5]. The maintenance conclusion identifies bearing wear as a recurring issue tied to lubricant contamination and vibration [S2].  

Not covered by the sources: the sources do not specify the exact sequence or timing of the three bearing-related events or whether misalignment was present in all instances.

results.question: How many major bearing events occurred for P-101?
results.answer: Three major bearing events occurred for P-101 [S1].

results.question: Which readings exceeded OEM limits?
results.answer:
Discharge pressure fell from 15 bar to 12 bar [S3]. Bearing temperature reached 108 C [S5]. Vibration reached 8.2 mm/s [S3] and 7.6 mm/s [S2]. Overall vibration limit is below 6.0 mm/s [S1]. Bearing temperature limit is below 90 C [S1]. Discharge pressure limit is 14 to 16 bar [S1].  

The readings that exceeded OEM limits are: bearing temperature at 108 C [S5], vibration at 7.6 mm/s and 8.2 mm/s [S2][S3], and discharge pressure dropping to 12 bar [S3].  

Not covered by the sources: the sources do not state whether the discharge pressure at 12 bar was below or above the 14 to 16 bar limit.

results.question: What maintenance was performed on 22-Nov-2025?
results.answer: On 22-Nov-2025, the maintenance team replaced the bearing and mechanical seal, flushed the bearing housing, and tested the pump [S1].

results.question: What did the lubricant sample show?
results.answer: The lubricant sample contained water and fine metallic particles [S1].

results.question: What safety steps apply before pump maintenance?
results.answer: Before pump maintenance, personnel must obtain an approved work permit [S1]. They must stop the equipment using the normal shutdown sequence [S1]. Electrical power must be isolated and lockout-tagout must be applied [S1][S2]. Process isolation valves must be closed and stored pressure must be released [S1][S2]. Zero energy must be verified before beginning work [S1]. Personnel must wear specified PPE and record the maintenance activity [S1].

results.question: What alert thresholds were recommended?
results.answer: The recommended alert thresholds were 6.0 mm/s vibration and 90°C bearing temperature [S1].

results.question: What was P-101 pressure after verification?
results.answer: Discharge pressure recovered to 15 bar at normal operating flow during verification [S2].

results.question: Did C-201 cause the P-101 failure?
results.answer: No, C-201 did not cause P-101 failure. The sources state that Compressor C-201 experienced a motor trip due to discharge temperature reaching 120°C, and no relation to Pump P-101 was found [S1]. Pump P-101 failures were independently attributed to bearing wear, lubricant contamination, high vibration, and temperature [S2][S3][S5]. There is no stated causal link between C-201 and P-101 operations or failures in the records [S1][S2][S3][S5]. The events are reported as separate incidents with no connection established.
